deadline_policy: Absolute deadline including setup and evaluation; stop at two completed epochs or the training deadline, whichever comes first. Reserve final time for evaluation and atomic checkpoint. Do not start late with a fresh full 7.5-hour budget.

training.backend: optimized C kernels after actual-trainer integration; existing PyTorch runner has different throughput
training.output_policy: Fresh dedicated run directory; preserve the previous stopped queue and checkpoints. No old 14-hour queue restart.

thermal_policy_to_implement.source: macOS ProcessInfo.thermalState; system thermal pressure, not a temperature or fire sensor
thermal_policy_to_implement.on_serious: Stop new training updates, best-effort atomic checkpoint, exit with thermal-stop reason.
thermal_policy_to_implement.on_critical: Stop compute immediately; preserve latest complete checkpoint. Do not continue evaluation/generation.
thermal_policy_to_implement.on_monitor_error: Stop training rather than treating missing monitoring as normal.
thermal_policy_to_implement.limitations: Software thermal monitoring does not certify battery/charger safety or prevent every possible fire.

readiness_requirements: Actual C epoch trainer with tested checkpoints, exact resume and validation.
Tested absolute-deadline and thermal-stop behavior; existing code does not yet provide this guard.
Observed 30-60 minute pilot, initially four requested CPU threads, including responsiveness and thermal state.
Physical check of battery, adapter and ventilated stable placement before unattended use.

observed_hardware_snapshot.pmset_report: No thermal or performance warning level recorded at inspection.
observed_hardware_snapshot.scope: Read-only current-state inspection, not a load test, hardware diagnosis or overnight safety certification.

timing_evidence_limits: Previous 7.42h two-epoch estimate used SIX requested threads and short low-load C observations. It does not predict this four-thread configuration or ensure completion by morning.
